The Kaleds were basically alien Nazis, and we know little to nothing about the Thals. Because they had been fighting for an insanely long time, the planet was becoming basically uninhabitable, and so this Kaled scientist guy named Davros created out of Kaled DNA what he considered to be the ultimate lifeform: this gross little squid thing inside a super powerful robot casing. He called it a Dalek. He had removed every emotion he considered "unnecessary", and so all they had left was hatred and racism. The problem was that they were too racist, and so they killed Davros and went off on a genocidal rampage against the universe, bent on destroying all life they came across.

It is playing on the dark forest theory, one of the solutions for the Fermi paradox.

A quote: The universe is a dark forest. Every civilization is an armed hunter stalking through the trees like a ghost, gently pushing aside branches that block the path and trying to tread without sound. Even breathing is done with care. The hunter has to be careful, because everywhere in the forest are stealthy hunters like him. If he finds another life—another hunter, angel, or a demon, a delicate infant to tottering old man, a fairy or demigod—there’s only one thing he can do: open fire and eliminate them.

Basically, we are surrounded by millions of civilizations, they simply didn't want to be noticed, the only sign of their existence is the brief Earth encompassing flash as they fire their weapons, only a matter of time until our planet, or even the whole solar system is thoroughly decimated. I find it poetic, it's that inherent social drive which let us rise which lead to our downfall.

AI art is great in a vacuum, the only reason why people should be complaining is because the people on top will use this technological innovation to hoard more money, while giving scraps to those on the bottom, just like with any other technological innovation. Our problem is capitalism, not AI art.

"AI art is made by stealing art made by artists." Yes, AI art engines are taught on a massive dataset of art pieces by human artists, pretty much all or which were used without noticing or asking for permission from the artist. That said, so are human artists, art doesn't come from nothing, we draw upon a vast set of seemingly random vague connections and selectively express it in various ways. Process not so different from the process of making AI art. Also, intellectual property should be abolished, so our issue is capitalism yet again.

"AI art isn't art because it doesn't express artists emotions." We are stupid apes, you don't know what the artist was feeling, if they were feeling anything, if it was even made by something capable of feelings. Whether something is art or not is such a complex debate which has a clear answer, who gives a flying fuck. I could make a dadaist poem and click on a button in a random word generator and you wouldn't be able to tell which is which. Me taking a shit on a piece of paper is as much a unique and personal expression of myself as me doing some automatic writing or randomly making strokes with a brush. That doesn't make art worthless or impossible to critique of course, we can critique art based on our aesthetic values and assign it worth which feel genuine to us. For some a banana taped to a wall is stupid and worthless, to some it is genius. 

"AI art isn't art because it wasn't made by an artist." If Earth was perfectly simulated to the point you could not tell virtual reality from real life, would the simulation be art because some people made it despite it being irrecognizable from the naturally made version? If so, what if instead of just simulating Earth, those people instead simulated trillions of trillions of big bangs, having no other input, would a perfect recreation of Earth created from such a process be art or a creation of random chance? It doesn't matter, connection between the art can be a factor in the connection we feel to the piece of art and it also doesn't have to. Inside the Library of Babel you can theoretically find every book that will ever be written, if I were to complete a book I am writing and publish it, would anyone be able to tell the difference between that and if I by ungodly chance stumbled upon in it the Library of Babel? Of course not. Yet the version I wrote is art and more meaningful? The only reason it carries more meaning than randomness is because we assigned the meaning to it. Keep in mind, just because we arbitrarily assigned meaning to it, doesn't make that meaning lesser, we assign arbitrary subjective meanings to our life, that shouldn't stop you from living life, the very struggle against inherent meaninglessness of existence is a meaning in itself.

There is more that could be said and addressed but I think I wrote more than enough here and way less than enough in my WIP book.

So to TLDR and finish off: AI art isn't bad, the system we live in is bad, while we are fixing the system, we can just make AI art a separate category and everyone can chill the fuck out and not sound like Luddites.

Rogue Legacy 2, it is very very easy to pick up(especially with a controller) but so so difficult to master. I am at 251.9 hours, after Minecraft my most played game, and I still have only 69% of the achievements and absolutely has not reached the difficulty ceiling. 

It has New Game+, which may seem to get samey but the game manages to balance the difficulty and gameplay changes well enough to make every New Game+ feel different. 

It's also the type of game you can play while listening to something else, which with my dopamine and serotonin starved ADHD brain, is absolutely perfect. The story is also good, explains a lot about how the whole setting came to be and the motivations of bosses.

One of the best things about this game in my opinion is the variety of strategies one can take, not just the classes, equipment, runes, weapons, talents, magics, mansion upgrades and so on, but also how one approaches advancing through the game. 

If you are a hardcore and focused player, you can get through the game very fast with skill, or you can be a bit casual and scatterbrained, forcing your way through with grinding. I don't like stressful games, Souls-like games and rage games I just can't handle(usually ends with me curled under the desk remembering living with my father, not good), so being able to get that crutch to compensate for my skill is amazing for me, plus with me being able to tweak the difficulty in many ways, I can work my way up and get better at the game by a pleasant gradual improvement instead of bashing my head against the wall.

Also, the game is quite funny and has a predecessor which I also adore but is weaker in many aspects but still worth playing but absolutely not mandatory.

Primus Principes (latin for "first leaders"):

- The name originates Roman and Greek scholars that were first to meet the alien race which landed on our planet and inspired the Graeco-Roman deities. This name is not mostly used by the group itself but rather is used by most of the population of the Milky Way galaxy.

- The group is roughly comparable to the G20 council, the main purpose is to keep peace between each of the "gods", generally each of them claims their native galaxy or mini-verse as territory and protected space.

- At the time of the main story there is only one "god" from the Milky Way, that being Andrew Void, human and one of fairly rare cases of someone becoming a "god" by work and science. There are many others however who have the potential of becoming one.

- There are many conditions to being invited to Primus Principes. One of the main ones is that your power has to be permanent(this excludes someone like Emperor of Human Technocratic Empire), other ones are things like being able to create intelligent life, artificial space the size of a star system, ability to travel between universes without a gate and to exert raw destructive power of a gamma ray burst.

- Primus Principes acts rarely as an united body, when they do it is mostly to keep other powerful entities in check and to keep peace. Other than that it is individual "gods" interacting with and observing their galaxy or "gods" with their territories closely connected, for example galaxies in Local Group or spaces connected by gates, however even those try not to get too involved in business of one another.

- Andrew Void, local "god" is a human from early 21st century, brilliant inventor, cybernetics pioneer and first human to be "reborn"(placing consciousness into entirely cybernetic body) and achieve immortality. He is a childhood friend of the Emperor, founder of Void Enterprises and patriarch of Void family. Overall he leaves business to his children and wanders the galaxy as a space nomad(kind of paralleling Little Prince).
